```{r, turning data into real date}
#turn all your date column into a real date
GE.2021.2022$Date = as.Date(GE.2021.2022$Date, "%m/%d/%y")
GE.2021.2022$Date

#Create "day" column for julian date for analysis
GE.2021.2022$day=yday(GE.2021.2022$Date)

#mean center
GE.2021.2022$mean.cent.day<-(GE.2021.2022$day)-(mean(GE.2021.2022$day))
#use "mean.center.day" from now on

#Write fundtion to make the times digestible by R. 
convert_to_seconds <- function(time_str) {
  if (is.na(time_str) || time_str == "") return(NA)  # Handle missing/blank values
  
  time_str <- trimws(time_str)  # Remove leading/trailing spaces
  
  # If the value is in HH:MM:SS format (Excel time of day)
  if (grepl("^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}$", time_str)) {
    parts <- as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(time_str, ":")))
    return(parts[1] * 3600 + parts[2] * 60 + parts[3])
  }
  
  # If the value is in MM:SS format (desired format)
  if (grepl("^\\d{1,2}:\\d{2}$", time_str)) {
    parts <- as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(time_str, ":")))
    return(parts[1] * 60 + parts[2])
  }
  
  # Handle numeric values (Excel stores time as a fraction of a day)
  suppressWarnings(num_val <- as.numeric(time_str))
  if (!is.na(num_val) && num_val < 1) {
    total_seconds <- num_val * 86400  # Convert fraction of a day to seconds
    return(round(total_seconds))  
  }
  
  return(NA)  # If format is unrecognized
}

# Apply the function to standardize times
GE.2021.2022 <- GE.2021.2022 %>%
  mutate(seconds = sapply(Time, convert_to_seconds))

#Filtering out all trials except late so we have a single data point per bird
GE.2021.2022.late = GE.2021.2022 %>% dplyr::filter(TRIAL=="Late")
```

```{r}
##geneXhabitat

l1= lmer(dd.ct ~ Habitat*GENE.x+mean.cent.day+Playback.exposure..mins.+(1|SAMPLE), data = GE.2021.2022)
#dropped mass and time of day (seconds) from the model using backwards stepwise
histogram(residuals(l1))
check_model(l1)
shapiro.test(residuals(l1))
summary(l1)
#using the anova function
anova(l1)
plot(allEffects(l1))
#Post hoc analysis
emm.l1<-emmeans(l1, ~ Habitat*GENE.x)
emm.l1
# For pairwise comparisons of all combinations
pairs(emm.l1)

# Or, for specific contrasts (e.g., comparing habitat within levels of gene target)
contrast(emm.l1, method = "pairwise", by = "GENE.x")

#exporting results
res.pro.table.1 <- as.data.frame(anova(l1))
res.pro.table.2 <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm.l1, method = "pairwise", by = "GENE.x"))
#write.csv(res.pro.table.1,"3.9.26.npy-r.geneXhabitat.results1.csv")
#write.csv(res.pro.table.2,"3.9.26.npy-r.geneXhabitat.results2.csv")
```

```{r}
##PCA of NPY-system genes (Supp. Mat. Fig. 2)

head(wide)
wide.late<-filter(wide, TRIAL == "Late")
#creating new dataset that only has NPY genes for PCA
wide.late.npy.genes <- wide.late |>
  dplyr::select(NPY, NPY1R, NPY2R, NPY5R)

#Handling missing values in PCA
#using packages labeled above^^(libraries)
nb<- estim_ncpPCA(wide.late.npy.genes, scale=TRUE)
comp<- imputePCA(wide.late.npy.genes, ncp=3, scale=TRUE)
res.pca <- PCA(comp$completeObs)

#graph of individual samples
fviz_pca_ind(res.pca, col.ind = "cos2", gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"), repel = TRUE)

#graph of variables (correlation circle)
supp.fig.3<-fviz_pca_var(res.pca, col.var = "contrib", gradient.cols = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800", "#FC4E07"), repel = TRUE)
supp.fig.3

#print fig for pub
ggsave("supp.fig.3.png", plot = supp.fig.3,
       width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 600)

# Biplot of individuals and variables
fviz_pca_biplot(res.pca, repel = TRUE)

#check your data
summary(res.pca)
#Explains 67.445%

#Add the PCA scores back into the data
wide.late$npy.genes = res.pca$ind$coord

#Write it into a data sheet and use this data sheet from now on
#write.csv(wide.late, ("NPY.genes.PCA.csv"))
```

```{r}
#PCA with only late aggression scores
#creating new dataset that only has aggressive signals so that I can run the permutation to deal with NAs
agg.late <- npy.pca.late |>
  select(No..soft.songs, Wing.wave, Distance..m.)
head(npy.pca.late)

#Handling missing values in PCA
#using packages labeled above^^(libraries)
nb.1<- estim_ncpPCA(agg.late, scale=TRUE)
comp.1<- imputePCA(agg.late, ncp=2, scale=TRUE)
res.pca.1 <- PCA(comp.1$completeObs)

#Add the PCA scores back into the data
npy.pca.late$AGG.late = res.pca.1$ind$coord
```

```{r}
#agg score is not normal, so I am transforming the data with log function
#Male agg score (AGG.late.Dim.1)
npy.pca.late$agg.t<-log(npy.pca.late$male.aggression)
npy.pca.late$agg.t

#looking at how the NPY system (PCA) relates to aggression
l2= lm(AGG.late.Dim.1~npy.genes.Dim.1+Habitat+mass, data= npy.pca.late)
histogram(l2$residuals)
check_model(l2)
shapiro.test(l2$residuals)
anova(l2)
summary(l2)

#exporting results
#res.pro.table.3 <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(l2)))
```

```{r}
#looking at how aggression relates to gene expression
#need to merge GE.2021.2022 (A) data sheet with npy.pca.late (B) data sheet because
#(A) has agg PC1 based on both early and late; (B) has just late included in PC1
#merging
merged_df <- merge(GE.2021.2022, npy.pca.late, by = "SAMPLE")
#transforming aggression score because it's not normal
merged_df$agg.t<-(merged_df$AGG.late.Dim.1+2)
merged_df$agg.t
merged_df$agg.t<-log(merged_df$agg.t)
merged_df$agg.t
head(merged_df)
l3= lm(agg.t~dd.ct.x*GENE.x.x+Habitat.x, data= merged_df )
histogram(l3$residuals)
check_model(l3)
shapiro.test(l3$residuals)
anova(l3)
#no effect of gene expression on aggression
```
